title: Zoom in: uploading a build as content-addressed chunks
caption: Like a multipart upload, chunks go up in parallel and are retried one by one, and a final commit makes the version exist. Unlike multipart, each chunk is its own object, so the next build can reuse it.

messages.label: chunk + SHA-256 every file
messages.note: Content-defined chunking: boundaries follow the bytes, so an edit early in a file shifts only the chunks around it, not every chunk after it.

messages.label: 7 040 known, 460 new
messages.note: Only about 4 GB of the 60 GB build is new.

messages.label: 460 presigned PUT URLs
messages.note: Each URL is bound to one key (the hash) and to a checksum header, and expires in an hour.

messages.label: PUT /chunks/<hash> × 460
messages.note: 32 at a time. A chunk that fails is retried on its own; the same key always holds the same bytes, so retries are harmless.

messages.label: HEAD the 460 new keys
messages.note: The publisher trusts the store, not the client: every chunk the manifest needs must exist before the version does.

messages.label: INSERT manifest 2.3.0
messages.note: Written once and never changed. 'live' still points at the old version until release.

scenarios.name: One chunk PUT fails
scenarios.summary: A dropped connection costs one 8 MB retry, and the commit check refuses a manifest with holes in it.

messages.label: connection reset on one
messages.note: The other chunks are complete objects already; nothing is lost but this one.

messages.label: commit 2.3.0
messages.note: Suppose CI has a bug and commits without retrying.

messages.label: rejected: 1 chunk missing
messages.note: The response names the hash, so CI uploads only that chunk.

scenarios.name: Two branches, same chunk
scenarios.summary: Two CI pipelines upload the same new chunk at the same moment. With content addressing, that race is harmless.

messages.label: begin hotfix 2.2.1
messages.note: Both builds contain the same new texture pack.

messages.label: PUT /chunks/9f2c… (hotfix)
messages.note: Last writer wins, but both wrote identical bytes, so the result is the same either way.

messages.label: 2 manifests, 1 shared chunk
messages.note: Stored once and referenced twice; garbage collection must count both references.

scenarios.name: Risk: reused chunk is cold
scenarios.summary: The index says a chunk exists, but lifecycle moved it to an archive tier hours away from being readable. Patch day would fail on it.

messages.label: known: 7 040
messages.note: One of them was last used three years ago and now sits in archive storage.

messages.label: HEAD each reused key
messages.note: The check reads each chunk's storage class, not just whether it exists.

messages.label: restore, then copy to hot
messages.note: An archive restore takes hours, so re-uploading it from CI as if it were new is often faster. Either way it must be hot before 'live' can point at this version.
